entries.1:1: Jude introduces himself as a servant of Jesus and brother of James, writing to people God has chosen, made holy, and kept safe for Jesus. It reminds you that you belong to God and are protected by him.
entries.1:2: Jude wishes his readers more mercy, peace, and love. It means God wants these good things to grow in your life.
entries.1:3: Jude wanted to write about the salvation we all share, but instead he urges believers to firmly defend the faith once given to God's people. It means you should hold firmly to the core truths of the faith.
entries.1:4: Some people had slipped in secretly who twist God's grace into an excuse for sin and deny Jesus as Master and Lord. It warns you that false teaching can enter quietly and must be recognized.
entries.1:5: Jude reminds them that the Lord rescued Israel from Egypt but later destroyed those who did not believe. It means past rescue does not excuse ongoing unbelief.
entries.1:6: Angels who abandoned their proper place are kept in chains in darkness until judgment day. It shows that even powerful beings face consequences for rebelling against God.
entries.1:7: Sodom, Gomorrah, and nearby towns pursued sexual immorality and unnatural desires and were punished as an example. It warns that God takes such sin seriously.
entries.1:8: These dreamers defile their bodies, reject authority, and insult heavenly rulers. It means the false teachers' immoral and disrespectful behavior reveals their true character.
entries.1:9: Even the archangel Michael, disputing with the devil over Moses' body, did not insult him but said the Lord would rebuke him. It shows that even high angels show restraint, so these men's arrogance is worse.
entries.1:10: These men insult what they don't understand and are destroyed by the things they follow by instinct like animals. It means their ignorance and unchecked instincts lead to ruin.
entries.1:11: Jude pronounces woe on them for following Cain's way, Balaam's greed, and Korah's rebellion. It means they repeat the destructive patterns of famous rebels against God.
entries.1:12: They are hidden rocks at your fellowship meals, selfishly feeding themselves, and are like waterless clouds and fruitless trees. It means they look promising but bring no good and cause damage.
entries.1:13: They are like wild waves foaming out shame and like wandering stars reserved for deepest darkness. It means their shameful lives lead to certain judgment.
entries.1:14: Enoch prophesied that the Lord would come with thousands of his holy ones. It means judgment on the ungodly is certain and was foretold long ago.
entries.1:15: The Lord comes to judge everyone and convict the ungodly for their evil deeds and harsh words against him. It means no ungodly action or word will escape God's judgment.
entries.1:16: These men grumble, complain, chase their own desires, boast loudly, and flatter others for advantage. It means their selfish and manipulative behavior marks them as false.
entries.1:17: Jude tells his dear friends to remember what the apostles of Jesus foretold. It means you should hold onto apostolic teaching as your guide.
entries.1:18: The apostles said that in the last days scoffers would come following their own ungodly desires. It means opposition to the faith is expected, not surprising.
entries.1:19: These men cause divisions, are worldly-minded, and lack the Spirit. It means their divisiveness shows they do not truly belong to God.
entries.1:20: Jude tells believers to build themselves up in their holy faith and pray in the Holy Spirit. It means you grow spiritually through faith and prayer.
entries.1:21: Keep yourselves in God's love while waiting for eternal life through Jesus' mercy. It means stay close to God and live in expectation of his mercy.
entries.1:22: Show mercy to those who are doubting. It means be compassionate toward people who struggle with their faith.
entries.1:23: Rescue some by snatching them from the fire, and show others mercy with caution, hating even the clothing stained by sin. It means help people out of danger while staying careful not to be pulled into sin yourself.
entries.1:24: God is able to keep you from stumbling and present you blameless before his glory with great joy. It means your security and final joy rest in God's power, not your own.
entries.1:25: To the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ, be glory, majesty, power, and authority before all time, now, and forever. It means God alone deserves all honor and praise eternally.
